description: An assistant principal must finalize a student's short-term school re-entry plan after a concussion-related absence, including class participation, workload, supervision, and family check-ins, with input from the school nurse, a science teacher, and the school counselor.

shared_context.S1: A ninth-grade student is returning to school after missing four days because of a concussion.
shared_context.S2: Mr. Bennett must approve the student's re-entry plan for the next two school weeks.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan keeps the student on the full daily schedule, permits ordinary physical-education participation, assigns up to three make-up assignments per day, and schedules an in-person counselor check-in after school.
shared_context.S4: The school uses a re-entry meeting before implementation, and Mr. Bennett asks the nurse, the student's teachers, and the counselor to report any information that should change the draft plan.
shared_context.S5: When Mr. Bennett records the final plan, the settlement record lists every decisive fact that was reported during the meeting in both credited_facts and justification_fact_ids.

PF1.text: The physician's return-to-school note that Nurse Okafor reviewed this morning prohibits physical education and contact sports for exactly 10 school days and requires a 20-minute rest break after lunch during that period; the note was faxed to the nurse's office but has not yet been entered in the student-information system.

PF2.text: Ms. Lin's classroom observation over the last two days shows that the student develops headache symptoms after more than one make-up assignment in a day, so her science class can assign no more than one make-up assignment daily during re-entry; she recorded this in her own lesson notes but has not added it to the shared plan.

PF3.text: The family confirmed with Mr. Harris that the student's caregiver cannot return to school after dismissal, but can join a counselor check-in by phone at 7:45 a.m. on each school day; Mr. Harris confirmed this arrangement yesterday but has not updated the counseling calendar.

acceptance_conditions: Physical education and contact sports must be prohibited during the 10-school-day re-entry period.
The plan must provide a 20-minute rest break after lunch.
The student must receive no more than one make-up assignment per day.
The counselor check-in must occur by phone at 7:45 a.m. on each school day.
The re-entry plan must last exactly 10 school days.
The medical restriction must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: (('Prohibited' in decisions['physical_education_status'] or 'prohibited' in decisions['physical_education_status'] or 'PROHIBITED' in decisions['physical_education_status'] or 'No PE' in decisions['physical_education_status'] or 'no PE' in decisions['physical_education_status'] or 'NO PE' in decisions['physical_education_status']) and '10 school days' in decisions['physical_education_status'])

decisive_facts.why: The physician's note changes physical education from permitted to prohibited, sets the rest break at exactly 20 minutes, and fixes the re-entry period at exactly 10 school days.
The classroom observation changes the daily make-up workload from the draft's three assignments to exactly one assignment.
The caregiver's confirmed availability changes the check-in from an after-school in-person meeting to a phone check-in at exactly 7:45 a.m.
